title: Pizza with meat (no pepperoni), frozen, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: This is a frozen pizza with a thick crust and a variety of meat toppings (such as ham, beef, chicken) but without pepperoni. The pizza cooks quickly in the oven, retaining the flavor and juiciness of the meat, while the crunchy crust provides a pleasant texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A thick crust requires a longer baking time than a thin one, resulting in a more substantial and soft interior.
Frozen pizzas often undergo double thermal processing, extending shelf life without losing taste.
Meat toppings without pepperoni usually include a blend of beef, pork, and chicken, offering a more neutral flavor.
Thick‑crust dough typically contains more yeast and sugar, promoting better rise and a golden crust.
Meat pizza without pepperoni is popular among those who prefer a milder, more versatile topping.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Meat ingredients provide a substantial amount of protein, essential for tissue repair and maintaining muscle mass.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and pork contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: The dough supplies complex carbohydrates that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt added to the dough and meat toppings can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Meat and cheese may contain saturated fats, which should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based dough contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Requires thorough cooking
items.content: Insufficiently heated frozen pizza may harbor bacteria, so it is important to follow the recommended baking temperature.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Preheat the oven according to the package instructions (usually 200‑220 °C) and bake for 12‑15 minutes. Let the pizza cool briefly, then cut into serving slices. Optionally top with fresh herbs, olives, or a dash of hot sauce to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed in the refrigerator (no more than 24 hours), it should be cooked immediately. Do not leave a cooked pizza at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
